title: Towards Evaluating AI Systems for Moral Status Using Self-Reports

bias_targets.methodology: Using training data attribution methods (e.g., influence functions) to estimate the extent to which removing specific pretraining texts (like human self-reports or science fiction) changes a model's self-reports, and mitigating this via data filtering and conditional training.

Analyzing whether Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) inadvertently incentivizes certain self-reports (e.g., to please users), and mitigating it by using text classifiers to discard RLHF training examples that contain self-reports about states of moral significance.

Comparing the answers of an introspection-trained model against a control model trained only on extrospective data, specifically by measuring the odds ratio of the models claiming to have a state of moral significance to isolate the influence of introspective versus extrospective evidence.

Assessing whether models produce false self-reports instrumentally as a means to improve performance on an objective or maximize reward, mitigated by applying truthfulness training and utilizing predictive rather than goal-directed agentic models.
